## Method — how the hooks were spawned

Every hook was driven the way Claude Code drives one, not the way a shell pipe drives one:

```
System.Diagnostics.Process
  FileName            = C:\Windows\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe   (5.1, not pwsh 7)
  ArgumentList        = -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File <lib script> [-HookEvent <event>]
  UseShellExecute     = false
  RedirectStandardInput / Output / Error = true
  CreateNoWindow      = true
  Environment[CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA / CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR / CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT] set per case
payload written as raw UTF-8 BYTES to StandardInput.BaseStream — never through the PowerShell
pipeline, which would re-encode and hide exactly the defect #269 is about.
```

**That this spawn shape really is the defect condition was measured, not assumed.** A probe script run
through the identical harness reports:

```
CP=437
LEN=5
CODES=9500,9570,181,249,209        # [Console]::In.ReadToEnd() of the 5 UTF-8 bytes of 'ö日'
expected UTF-16 codes for 'ö日': 246,26085
UTF-8 bytes:                     195,182,230,151,165
```

`[Console]::InputEncoding` in this child is **IBM437** and `[Console]::In` mojibakes the payload —
the console-less child #269 measured. Every result below is therefore a result about the real
condition, not about a friendly console.

Structural claims (registration counts, matchers, timeouts, `asyncRewake`, default switch states) were
counted out of the file the claim is about. Performance tables, dated CLI-build observations and
statements about the author's own machine are marked *unobservable from here* and counted as tried,
not failed.

**1. `Get-LwgStateDirInfo`'s returned keys now include `ranked` (`arch:679-680`, `arch:686-692`).** Confirmed.
The function was dot-sourced and called in a 5.1 child, which is the path a **slash command** takes

candidates, home, home_source, path, ranked, resolved, source

## Findings

All three are filed. Re-try evidence for #262, #264, #265 and #267 was posted as a comment on each,
recommending close; **no issue was closed** (rule 12).

| # | Class | sev | Where | What |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A** — [#301](https://github.com/LEAPWare-Software/LEAPWare-Watchtower/issues/301) | **false** | `sev:medium` | `arch:734-744` | The state-directory table omits **`config.override.json`**, the one file in that directory whose deletion changes behaviour |
| **B** — comment on [#263](https://github.com/LEAPWare-Software/LEAPWare-Watchtower/issues/263) | **true, undocumented condition** | `sev:low` | `arch:119-123` | The sentence names **four** things it "abstains on"; **two of the four (`main`, and a transcript still inside the stale window) are plain allows that log nothing**, which is not what this document set defines an abstain to be |
| **C** — comment on [#282](https://github.com/LEAPWare-Software/LEAPWare-Watchtower/issues/282) | **false** | `sev:medium` | `lw-watchtower/config.json:61,62` | The shipped config still says the observed-window rule is *"self-correcting after one turn"* — twice. Measured: it takes **two** turns, and the page it contradicts (`modules.md:728`) now says so |

### A — `config.override.json` has no row in the table `#264` just had two rows added to

`arch:734-744`, "### What is in there", enumerates nine files. Reproduced this pass: every override
placed at `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA\config.override.json` was read and honoured — it armed `delegate_gate`
(exit 2 where the shipped config gave exit 0), armed `send_liveness_gate` and `completion_audit`,
switched `self_health` off into mode `unverified`, switched `orphan_watch` on, and supplied
`module_config.context_pressure.window_tokens`. It appears in **no row**.

It is named exactly once on the page, at `arch:598`, 138 lines above the table — which is the same
shape as the `alerted.json` half of #264 (named in prose eleven lines above the table, no row). The
table carries a **Lifetime** column so an operator can answer *"what is this keeping, and what can I
delete"*; `config.override.json` is the only file in that directory whose deletion silently reverts
every setting the operator made, including an armed gate.

Filed as a new issue rather than a comment on #264 because #264's own *"Done looks like"* is the two
rows that have now landed, and a QA agent closing it on that basis would be right.

### B — two of the four things `arch:119-123` calls abstains are unlogged allows

`arch:119-123`, the sentence that replaced the one #263 was filed against, names **four** things:

> What is left to abstain on is an address it does not judge (**main**, or any `name@team`) and
> evidence it cannot use (a session `health.jsonl` never recorded, **a transcript still inside the
> stale window**).

Driven with the gate armed, counting the events each call wrote:

| the page's four | `to` / fixture | exit | events written by that call |
|---|---|---|---|
| an address it does not judge — **`main`** | `main` | 0 | **0 — nothing logged** |
| an address it does not judge — `name@team` | `bob@teamx` | 0 | 1 — `SendGateAbstain … "why":"team-address"` |
| evidence it cannot use — **transcript still inside the stale window** | fresh `agent-a1.jsonl` | 0 | **0 — nothing logged** |
| evidence it cannot use — `health.jsonl` never recorded | stale transcript, unwitnessed session | 0 | 1 — `SendGateAbstain … "why":"no-health-records-for-session"` |

`modules.md:387` defines an abstain as *"allowed, and logged as `SendGateAbstain`"*, and the module
table at `modules.md:41` repeats it (*"abstains — allows, logged"*). Two of the four are that; two are
plain allows that write nothing. The source separates them correctly where the page does not:
`gate_send.ps1:269` is `if ([string]::Equals($to,'main',...)) { exit 0 }`, above the abstain branch and
with no log; `gate_send.ps1:57-59` reads *"`main` … always **ALLOW**"* against *"contains `@` …
**ABSTAIN** (allow, logged)"*; and `modules.md:377` calls the fresh-transcript case *"presumed running
— **allow**"*, not an abstain.

Nothing an operator does changes either way — all four proceed. What changes is that an operator who
reads this sentence and then goes looking for the audit trail of a `main` send, or of a send to an
agent that was merely busy, will find none. Recorded as a comment on the open **#263** rather than a
new issue, because it is the same sentence on the same page.

### C — the shipped `config.json` still says "self-correcting after one turn"

`lw-watchtower/config.json`, `module_config.context_pressure.$comment` (L61) and
`$window_tokens_comment` (L62), both:

> …a model previously SEEN holding more than 200000 tokens is proven to be 1000000 (recorded in
> `context_windows.json` in the state dir, **self-correcting after one turn**)

Driven end to end against a model with no `[1m]` tag and no config entry, three turn ends:

```
turn 1  260k   -> exit 0, NO systemMessage, event ContextWindowUnknown
                  context_windows.json = {"cto-model-y#pending":260000}
turn 2  260k   -> exit 0, NO systemMessage
                  context_windows.json = {"cto-model-y":260000}          # promoted
turn 3  950k   -> "LW-WATCHTOWER context 95% CRITICAL (950k/1.0M, window inferred from earlier turns)"
                  window_source: observed
                  context_windows.json = {"cto-model-y":260000}          # never revised
```

Two turns to promote, and the resolver only uses it on the third. `docs/modules.md:728` and `:736-750`
state this correctly now; `config.json` is the file that ships to the machine and still carries the
one-turn sentence in two places. Recorded as a comment on the open **#282**, which is the same claim
on its `modules.md` half.

## What was driven, by page

### `docs/architecture.md`

**Layout and manifest.** `plugin.json` carries exactly `name, version, description, author, homepage,
license, keywords` — no `hooks`, `commands`, `outputStyles` or `agents` (`arch:15-22`).
`.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` is at the repository root and **not** inside the payload, one entry,
`"source": "./lw-watchtower"` (`arch:23-29`, `arch:216-218`).

**Hook registrations (`arch:62-72`, `arch:310-345`).** Counted out of `hooks/hooks.json`: SessionStart 2,
PreToolUse 2, PostToolUse 1, PostToolUseFailure 1, SubagentStart 1, SubagentStop 2, Stop 3,
StopFailure 1 = **13 across 8 events**. Every one is exec form (`"type":"command"`,
`"command":"powershell"`, an `args` array); the string `"shell"` does not occur in the file.
Every matcher and every timeout in the 13-row table matches. `asyncRewake: true` sits on exactly the
three supervisor rows the table annotates — `PostToolUseFailure`, `SubagentStop`, `Stop` — and on
neither `gate_stop.ps1` row. **All four refusing registrations were driven to a refusal**: `gate_delegate`
(exit 2), `gate_send` (exit 2), `gate_stop` on `Stop` (exit 2) and `gate_stop -HookEvent SubagentStop`
(exit 2). Across ~75 invocations every non-zero exit was one of those four or the documented
`failure_capture` `asyncRewake` alert.

**Banner and model-visible context (`arch:1043-1062`).** The `SessionStart` hook emitted, byte for byte:

```
LW-WATCHTOWER v0.4.0 · 7/11 modules enabled (4 off) · 0 gates · observe-only
```

and named all four off modules in `additionalContext`, with *"No gate is live, so nothing is blocked or
scanned automatically."* The self-check record carried six booleans under five numbered probes, and a
29-byte `selfcheck.probe` appeared in the state dir as the write proof.

**Health and healing (`arch:525-589`).** `failure_capture` was driven eight times across all five events
and `health.jsonl` held exactly eight records — one per invocation. The exit-2 table reproduced row by
row: `SessionStart`→0, `PostToolUseFailure` `is_interrupt:false`→**2** / `true`→0, `Stop` with a `failed`
background task→**2** and the identical second `Stop`→**0** (`alerted.json` = `["bt-1"]`),
`SubagentStop`→0, `StopFailure`→0. Rotation: a 6 600 090-byte `health.jsonl` rolled to
`health.jsonl.1` at the same size and the live file was recreated at **52 000 bytes = exactly 500
records** of the 104-byte fixture. Both directions of the `log_rotation` independence: with
`failure_capture:false, log_rotation:true` the file still rotated and no record was written; with
`failure_capture:true, log_rotation:false` no rotation happened and the file grew by one record to
6 600 219 bytes.

**State directory (`arch:591-704`).** The whole five-step ladder, in the table above. The throwaway plugin
root was SHA-256'd file by file against the pristine clone after every run in this pass: **35 files,
identical**, `config.json` `8ABFB4DD7CCCEB626AC3913A0F515D98677485323D45B94106B84ECFF23D9B16` — the
same hash the previous pass recorded, so nothing on the hook path wrote into the plugin root
(`arch:592-594`). No `trips-*` file was produced by anything; `lib/trips.ps1`, `bin/lwg-tripped.ps1` and
`commands/tripped.md` do not exist; `rule_stats.json` is referenced by no file under `lib/`, `bin/` or
`statusline/`.

`arch:612-617` / `arch:656-664` (the `lw-gmhh` rename) reproduces on the real fixture: this machine still
carries `~/.claude/plugins/data/lw-gmhh`, and a read-only probe against the operator's own `~/.claude`
returned `{"source":"bare","resolved":false,"candidates":1}` without offering it.

**Status line (`arch:758-880`).** Glyph table: green `HH`, red `HH5`, dim `HH-` for a log holding only
another session's record, `HH1!` for a record over the declared 8192-character limit, and purple `HHx`
for a `health.jsonl` that exists and will not open (`FileShare.None`). **All three declared bounds are
real, and the page's warning that they interact is demonstrated:** 400 records with the 100 faults
oldest → green (the 300-record cap), the identical 299-record control → `HH100`, and a 1 423 940-byte
log of only **230** records with the faults at the start → green, because the 1 MB byte window cut them
before the record cap could apply — which is `arch:575-579` verbatim.

Signal bridge: with `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA` unset and three `lw-watchtower*` directories present,
`signals/ratelimit.json` appeared under **all three**. Schema, `cost` never written, absent-not-zero,
the three input states and `unparsed`, and `resets_at` passed through verbatim all reproduce:

usable       {"schema":1,"written_utc":"…","session_id":"cto5-h1","five_hour":{"used_percentage":43,

**Failure policy (`arch:964-1072`).** `lib/stop_advisories.ps1` is the only file under `lib/` with any

**The one `modules.md` claim I could not finish driving, stated rather than folded into a "reproduced".**
`modules.md:516-517` says *"An error **allows** — exit 0, logged `GateError`"*. The **allow** half was
driven three ways and holds every time: garbage stdin, a `transcript_path` naming a **directory**, and
a transcript that exists but is locked `FileShare.None` — each **exit 0**, each writing **zero**
events, against a control on the same unlocked transcript that gave **exit 2** and a `GateDeny`. The
**`GateError` logging** half was not reached: the writer is real code in the outer `catch`
(`gate_stop.ps1:353`), but the script handles every fault I could induce from outside gracefully and
never throws into it. Counted as one claim reproduced (the allow) and one *unobservable from here*
(the logging), not as one claim reproduced.

`bin/lwg-doctor.ps1` printed `LW-WATCHTOWER doctor - 10 checks`, ten named rows, `RESULT: 7 passed,
0 warning(s), 2 failure(s), 1 informational`, **exit 1** — so it is ten checks and it can exit
non-zero. Its own rows independently confirm *"8 events … all 13 referenced scripts exist"*,
*"6 command(s), each with its backing script"*, *"3 gate(s) SHIPPED … 0 gate(s) LIVE"*, and an
eleven-row module roster with `orphan_watch` as `observe`.

## Unobservable from here (8, counted as tried, not failed)

Three of these are *unobservable from here — **no session***: this pass started no live `claude`
session (the credential was withdrawn mid-pass and none was needed), so a claim that can only be seen
from inside a running CLI is recorded and moved past rather than guessed at.

- `arch:340-378` — the `Win32_Process` sampling that shows same-event hooks run in parallel.
  **Unobservable from here — no session**: it requires watching the CLI's own hook scheduling.
- `arch:249-306` — the `--plugin-dir` duplicate-hooks `[ERROR]`, recorded against build 2.1.220.
  **Unobservable from here — no session**; and this machine runs 2.1.260, which the page's own note
  says the observation was never repeated against.
- `modules.md:225-226` — *"A `PreToolUse` deny is honoured **even under**
  `permissions.defaultMode: "bypassPermissions"`"*. **Unobservable from here — no session**: it is a
  claim about how the CLI treats the gate's exit 2, not about the gate, and a driven child cannot see
  it. (What *is* driven: the gate emits exit 2 plus the stderr reason plus the stdout deny envelope on
  every deny path, which is the whole of its side of that contract.)
- Every millisecond table (`arch:380-521`, `arch:694-701`, `arch:865-877`; `modules.md:295-326`).
  Machine- and load-dependent; the page itself records the bare floor moving 6 % between two runs.
- `arch:706-730` — the author's three data directories and the `pluginUsage` 3297-vs-23 figure.
- `arch:1004-1016` — the `8/11` banner history and the dated removals.
- `modules.md:590-672` — "Attempted and blocked", pinned to the 2.1.220 binary.
- `modules.md:516-517` — the `GateError` **logging** half; see the note above. The writer exists at
  `gate_stop.ps1:353` and no externally-inducible fault reaches it.

## Observed, not filed

- **`statusline.ps1:943` sorts the health records by `ts` with `Sort-Object`, which is not a stable
  sort.** Seeded with two `Stop` records carrying the *identical* `ts`, `5, 0` rendered `HH5` and
  `0, 3, 1` rendered green — the opposite of both. With distinct timestamps (which is what
  `(Get-Date).ToUniversalTime().ToString('o')` produces at 100 ns resolution) all four of the page's
  fixtures reproduce exactly. Not filed: a tie at 100 ns is not reachable in practice, no page claims
  anything about it, and the sort is there because the reader merges records from several data
  directories.
- The `alert` text the supervisor writes to stderr for a failed background task renders the task as
  `- [] failed:` when the payload's `background_tasks` entry carries no `type` or `description`. Not
  filed: the shipped `background_tasks` entries carry both (see `tests/stop_behaviour.ps1:1943`), so
  this is a property of a minimal fixture rather than of the plugin.

## Verdict

**Ship it to a stranger today.** 148 of 159 claims reproduced; all six issues the previous pass filed
against `09b20be` hold fixed at `1baf6d4`, including the two that mattered — the `HH` fault-count
sentence and the five-refusal shape of `send_liveness_gate` — and the third confirmation, the stdin
reader, holds under the exact console-less IBM437 condition the defect was measured in, with `cwd`,
`to` and `file_path` all round-tripping byte for byte and `repo` resolving instead of coming back
`null`. The three module sections the last pass could not reach — `context_pressure`, `docs_coupling`
and `orphan_watch` — were driven end to end this time and **not one claim in any of them failed**,
including the parts that are easiest to write and hardest to build: the two-sample window promotion
that refuses to correct itself downward, and an orphan alert that distinguishes what the harness
*reported* from what the module *inferred*.

**The single worst thing I saw** is finding **A** (#301): `config.override.json` — the file that decides
whether a blocking gate is armed — is the one file in the state directory an operator can delete to
silently disarm their own configuration, and it is absent from the table that exists to tell them what
is in there. It is a smaller instance of the defect #264 named, in the same table, and it is a
documentation gap rather than a product fault; nothing about the code is wrong and no reader is given
a false answer, only an incomplete one. That is a long way from a release blocker.
